newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed flat to slightly higher after a quiet featureless session, ticking up in late trade to erase earlier modest losses.
Dealers said the European Union's two-day Amsterdam summit had failing to provide any trading leads.
"The summit produced a weak compromise which was exactly what the market expected," said one dealer.

The bloc's euro currency would probably be launched on time, but it would be a soft currency and this meant peripheral EU bond markets such as Spain and Italy would probably outperform the core markets linked to Germany, he added.

Debt markets were expected to drift along close to current levels in the coming weeks with volatility increasing as the July 1 and 2 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee to consider U.S. interest rates approaches.
"I think the possibility of another U.S. rate rise has becoming less likely. I think that when the Fed raised rates in March it was meant to last for the whole year," a dealer said.
Dealers were largely dismissive of recent reports of strong Dutch growth stoking inflation and pushing up bond yields.
"The very tight supply of new government bonds will prevent Dutch yields from creeping up too much," said one.
